name: isPolyAInPolyB
formula: =LAMBDA(verticesA,verticesB,LET(n, ROWS(verticesA), mids, HSTACK(MAP(SEQUENCE(n), LAMBDA(i, (INDEX(verticesA, i, 1) + INDEX(verticesA, IF(i = n, 1, i + 1), 1)) / 2)), MAP(SEQUENCE(n), LAMBDA(i, (INDEX(verticesA, i, 2) + INDEX(verticesA, IF(i = n, 1, i + 1), 2)) / 2))), AND({ref}IsAllPointsInPoly(verticesB, verticesA), {ref}IsAllPointsInPoly(verticesB, mids))))
comment: Returns TRUE when polygon A lies inside polygon B, including when A touches the boundary or equals B. VerticesA and verticesB are n×2 arrays of (x, y) rows; the last row connects to the first. Each vertex of A and the midpoint of each edge of A must lie inside or on B. A vertex of A outside B returns FALSE. Fewer than two columns returns #REF!. Last Update at 2026-11-03.
